## 1. Learning objectives
By the end you can:
- install the JDK and confirm the version;
- write and run a program that prints text;
- explain the parts of a basic Java program in your own words;
- run automated tests and read a red/green result.

## 2. Plain-English explanation
- **Java** is a programming language. You write instructions in a text file; the **JDK** (Java Development
  Kit) turns them into something your computer runs.
- A **class** is a named container for code. Our app starts in a class called `Main`.
- A **method** is a named block of steps. `main` is special: Java starts running there.
- `System.out.println("...")` prints a line of text. Text in quotes is a **String**.
- A method can **return** a value. `banner()` returns the title text; `main` prints it. Separating
  "make the text" from "print the text" lets us **test** the text automatically.
- A **test** is code that checks your code. Green = the check passed. Red = it did not.

## 3. Runnable sample code
`examples/HelloJava.java`:
```java
public class HelloJava {
    public static void main(String[] args) {
        System.out.println("Hello, Java!");
        System.out.println("I am going to build an Inventory & Sales System.");
    }
}
```
Run it (no build tool needed):
```
java lessons/01-hello-java/examples/HelloJava.java
```

1. Install the JDK (see [docs/SETUP.md](https://github.com/rvirayii-est/java-by-building/blob/main/docs/SETUP.md)). Run `java -version` — expect `21`.
2. Open `starter/src/main/java/dev/javabybuilding/inventory/Main.java`.
3. Find `TODO 1`. Make `banner()` return exactly `=== Inventory & Sales System ===`
   (Hint: `return "=== Inventory & Sales System ===";`).
4. From the `starter` folder run the tests: `../../../mvnw test` (Windows: `..\..\..\mvnw.cmd test`).
   Before your change: **1 failure** (`bannerHasTheApplicationName`). After: all green.
5. Run the program (the test command already compiled it). From `starter`:
   `java -cp target/classes dev.javabybuilding.inventory.Main`

## 5. Practical exercises
Work in `exercises/` (open `Exercises01.java`, make `Exercises01Test` pass):
1. `greet(name)` → `"Hello, Ana!"` for `"Ana"`.
2. `receiptHeader(shopName)` → `"*** MANG TOMAS STORE ***"` for `"Mang Tomas Store"`
   (Hint: strings have `.toUpperCase()`).
3. *Stretch:* print your own name and favourite product from a new `main` method.

## 6. Expected results

```
=== Inventory & Sales System ===

```
`solution` module: **4 tests, 0 failures.** (`starter`: 1 failing until TODO 1 is done.)

## 7. Common mistakes and troubleshooting
| Symptom | Cause | Fix |
|---|---|---|
| `'java' is not recognized` / `command not found` | JDK not installed or not on PATH | Reinstall the JDK; reopen the terminal |
| `error: class X is public, should be declared in a file named X.java` | File name differs from class name | Rename the file or class so they match exactly |
| `';' expected` | Missing semicolon at the end of a statement | Add `;` |
| Test says `expected: <...> but was: <>` | Method still returns `""` | Replace the placeholder with the right text |
| Test fails on one character | Typo or extra space in the string | Compare character by character; strings must match exactly |
| `Unsupported class file major version` | Running with an older Java | `java -version` must be 21 |
